question: Which of the following compounds is formed when lead nitrate is mixed with potassium iodide?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lead iodide**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **yellowish solid** precipitates when a solution of **potassium iodide** is added to a solution of **lead nitrate** that has been taken in a test tube.
 
• **Lead iodide** is this opalescent solid. Lead iodide and **potassium nitrate** are created together.
 
• **Iodide** ions **displace** **nitrate** from lead nitrate and nitrate replaces iodine from potassium iodide when aqueous lead nitrate is introduced.
 
• As a result, potassium nitrate and lead iodide, two **new compounds**, are created. This is an illustration of a d**ouble displacement reaction**.
 
• Additionally, the things produced have an **odd colour**. Lead nitrate is yellow in colour while potassium nitrate is white when it is created.
 
• The **Precipitate** produced is the chemical compound **lead iodide**.
 
• *Therefore, lead iodide is formed when lead nitrate is mixed with potassium iodide.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **Compound**
 **Properties**
 
 

 **Lead carbide**
 A hypothetical chemical **combination** of** lead** and **carbon** is called **lead carbide**. Even at extremely high temperatures, lead and carbon do not typically mix.
 
 

 **Lead nitride**
 White, **crystalline** lead nitrate is **solid**. The substance **dissolves** in **water**. Although it is **noncombustible**, it will quicken the combustion of combustible substances.
 
 

 **Lead oxide** 
 A class of **inorganic** substances having the chemical formulae **lead** and** oxygen** is called **lead oxide**. Lead oxide is a well-known significant **industrial substance** that has been extensively used in batteries.
